headline: A Provost's AI-Written Op-Eds, a16z's College Alternative, and California's Push for an AI "Kill Switch"
thesis: A Dartmouth investigation finds the provost's own opinion pieces score a median 96% AI-written on the detector Pangram -- including a column urging colleges to catch student AI cheating -- the same week Andreessen Horowitz opens a $42 million unaccredited AI academy as a college alternative and California's governor pushes toward an AI "kill switch."
summary: The week's sharpest irony comes out of Dartmouth, where student journalists ran the provost's published writing through the AI detector Pangram and found a median AI-written score of 96% -- including a Washington Post column in which Provost Santiago Schnell urged colleges to move beyond simply catching students who cheat with AI. It lands the same week NYC's nation-leading K-12 generative-AI moratorium keeps drawing fire: EdTech Digest argues the ban through eighth grade won't work, even as Brookings makes the case for schools to "go slow to go fast" on AI adoption instead. Higher ed's alternative-pathways debate got louder too, as Andreessen Horowitz opened applications for its $42 million unaccredited Horowitz Andreessen Academy, an AI-era college alternative backed by Anthropic, Google, Meta, Nvidia, Palantir and OpenAI. Regulators are moving in parallel -- California Governor Newsom's new executive order pushes frontier AI labs toward independent, onsite verification and an AI "kill switch," with recommended legal changes due November 16. On the operations side, EdTech Magazine flags the IT-budgeting fallout of the AI boom: K-12 districts weighing what workloads belong in the cloud versus on-prem, and university IT leaders bracing for volatile, consumption-based AI pricing. And fall's conference marathon is now just days out -- EDUCAUSE's annual conference opens September 29, CBExchange follows September 30-October 3, and EdTech Week returns to Columbia's Teachers College October 13-15.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · September 24, 2026 · Items were sourced and dated via web-search indexing rather than live page fetches this run (direct fetches to source sites were blocked by network egress restrictions); Education Technology Insights, 1EdTech, EdTech Week, Ed-Fi and ISTE had no September-dated coverage surface in search, so their most relevant recent items are listed instead with a note.

themes.title: Dartmouth Provost's AI-Written Op-Eds Ignite a Campus Reckoning on Authenticity
themes.body: Student journalists ran Provost Santiago Schnell's published opinion pieces and academic articles through the AI detector Pangram and found a median AI-written score of 96%, including a Washington Post column that urged colleges to move beyond catching student AI cheating.

themes.title: NYC's Nation-Leading Generative AI Moratorium Keeps Fueling Debate
themes.body: EdTech Digest argues the city's ban on student-facing generative AI through eighth grade won't work, even as Brookings makes the case that schools should "go slow to go fast" on AI adoption rather than rushing in or shutting it out entirely.

themes.title: California Pushes Independent Oversight and a Kill Switch for Frontier AI
themes.body: Governor Newsom's new executive order directs experts to recommend embedding independent verification organizations onsite at frontier AI labs and advancing an AI "kill switch," with proposed legal changes due November 16.

themes.title: Andreessen Horowitz Bets $42M on an Unaccredited AI Academy as a College Alternative
themes.body: The venture firm's Horowitz Andreessen Academy, backed by Anthropic, Google, Meta, Nvidia, Palantir and OpenAI, has opened applications for ambitious 16-to-22-year-olds seeking an AI-era alternative to a traditional degree.

themes.title: K-12 and Higher Ed IT Leaders Grapple With Cloud and AI Cost Decisions
themes.body: EdTech Magazine weighs which K-12 workloads belong in the cloud versus on-prem, while urging university IT leaders to build usage caps and monitoring dashboards to survive volatile, consumption-based AI pricing.

themes.title: Fall's Conference Marathon Opens Next Week
themes.body: EDUCAUSE's annual conference opens September 29, CBExchange follows September 30-October 3, and EdTech Week returns to Columbia's Teachers College October 13-15.
